oil.summary: Crude markets remain gripped by Middle East supply-risk premium. WTI surged 5.93% on the day to $91.99/bbl — up 25.6% on the month — though the headline today noted prices topping $98 intraday, consistent with the sharp intraday range. Brent's 7.49% single-day decline to $87.02 likely reflects a roll or settlement anomaly against what the news flow describes as a relentless rally toward $100. The geopolitical stack is formidable: U.S. strikes on Iran entered a 12th consecutive night, Houthi forces targeted two Saudi tankers in Bab el-Mandeb forcing diversions, and Ukrainian drones struck a Russian refinery and pumping station. Iran's threatened oil blockade has already rerouted Gulf exports, pushing India to deepen Russian crude ties and prompting refiners to bypass traders and source Venezuelan barrels directly. Heating oil's 34.3% monthly surge underlines tight distillate balances.
drivers: 12 consecutive nights of U.S. strikes on Iran plus Houthi tanker attacks in Bab el-Mandeb driving acute supply-disruption premium
Gulf export rerouting forcing India to pivot to Russian and Latin American crude, while refiners cut out traders to source Venezuelan barrels directly
Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian refinery and pumping station adding further upstream/midstream supply risk

gas.summary: European gas dominated the tape: TTF has surged 47.2% over the past month to €61.86/MWh, though it eased 1.08% today. Equinor CEO Anders Opedal warned Wednesday that Europe may miss its winter storage target, adding a structural bearish undertone to near-term filling ambitions. EU sanctions negotiations produced a messy compromise — Greek Dynagas secured an exemption on Russian LNG cargoes, and Russian gas shipments remain broadly exempt from the new package, highlighting the bloc's continued dependence. Separately, Middle East war disruption is eroding Qatar's and UAE's LNG pricing leverage as importers push for lower contract prices. Henry Hub was essentially flat at $2.944/MMBtu (+0.68%), with new Permian pipeline capacity expected to alleviate persistent associated-gas oversupply in the basin.
drivers: Equinor CEO warning Europe risks missing winter storage targets, sustaining TTF's sharp monthly rally
EU sanctions deal exempts Russian gas cargoes and Greek Dynagas, underscoring European dependence on Russian supply despite geopolitical pressure
Middle East war reducing Qatar and UAE LNG pricing power as importers demand concessions, while new Permian pipelines signal eventual relief for U.S. gas glut

power.summary: Power and carbon newsflow is thin today. EU Carbon (EUA) slipped 2.08% to $80.07/EUA on the day but remains up 7.1% on the week and 4.7% on the month — modest moves relative to the energy complex broadly. TTF's elevated level at €61.86/MWh continues to weigh on European power generation economics. The only sector-specific headline of note is India's solar manufacturing setback: local panel factories have begun shutting due to component shortages, a meaningful setback for the country's renewable buildout ambitions. U.S. refinery utilization hitting 96.2% is relevant context for tight fuel markets globally but is primarily an oil-sector data point. Overall, direct power and carbon catalysts in today's feed are limited.
drivers: EU EUA edged down 2.08% on the day despite remaining elevated on the week, with high TTF prices keeping gas-fired generation economics under pressure
India's solar manufacturing disruption — factory shutdowns due to component shortages — threatens renewable capacity expansion targets
Thin direct power/carbon headlines today; sector largely trading in the shadow of broader energy complex tightness driven by Middle East conflict
